//: Ask AI's buttons, one entry per action kind. Read by src/main/help-assistant.js (the ACTIONS lines in the prompt, the reply cleaner and its params check, role gating) and src/renderer/src/studio-actions.js (what each button runs and whether this role may run it), so the two can't drift apart. Fields: label = how the model should word the button; target = what the action's target names, resolved to an id on the server (src/main/index.js helpResolveActions; see targets); params = the 'key=value' strings it takes, by type (see paramTypes); methods = every API method the button ends up calling, and a role needs all of them (none = it only opens a place, which the layout's own access checks); needs = an extra right from the Prompt Library (promptView, promptEdit) or a connection (googleDrive); spends = paid work, always confirmed with an estimate; destructive = confirmed as a danger; confirm = none | dialog | estimate | handoff (a dialog elsewhere has the last word) | card (a card under the answer has the button); form = when an action form card lets the person check what Ask AI filled in (always | params | never); layouts = where it works; prompt = the model's instruction line. test/ask-actions-registry.test.js keeps every method real and every kind wired.

paramTypes.text:N: plain text up to N characters
paramTypes.channels: channel names or ids separated by |, mapped to this workspace's channel ids
paramTypes.date: YYYY-MM-DD within a year of today
paramTypes.url: an http(s) address the person wrote themselves
paramTypes.emails: email addresses the person wrote themselves, separated by | or commas, up to 50

targets.question: a question to send (not resolved)
targets.trend.waiting: a trend still waiting for a decision (runId and themeId)
targets.trend.decided: a trend decided while its run still waits for review (runId and themeId)
targets.trend.ready: a trend whose report is ready (themeId)
targets.report: a written report outside channel asset sets (assetId)
targets.asset: a report, or a channel asset file as "Folder › File" (assetId)
targets.folder: a channel asset folder (folderKey = its kit source key)
targets.run.stopped: a failed, partial or stopped run (runId)
targets.prompt: a prompt in the Prompt Library (promptId)
targets.any: anything with a name: report, folder, trend, program, run, prompt or page (ref = { kind, id })
targets.who: a role or a person in the team (roleId, or memberId)

start-research.label: Start research with “<program>”
start-research.prompt: target = a program name from programs. Starts a research run with that program's whole saved setup (Apify and AI; they confirm the estimate first). It can't be narrowed to one topic: for one topic, offer quick-scan.

quick-scan.label: Run a small scan on <topic> (last 6 hours)
quick-scan.prompt: target = the topic. Offers a quick scan: a small, hour-level look at recent posts on that topic from a research program's saved accounts. Fill scan (see QUICK SCANS) and pair it with a scan-plan card, where they check the cost and start it.

approve-trend.label: Yes to “<trend>”
approve-trend.prompt: target = a trend name from trends.waiting. Says yes to it. params: note=<a note for the channels> and channels=<names from channels, separated by |> when they asked to route it; run=<that row's run> when two waiting rows share the name. With a note or channels they check it on a card first.

pass-trend.label: Skip “<trend>”
pass-trend.prompt: target = a trend name from trends.waiting. Skips it. params: note=<why> when they gave a reason; run=<that row's run> when two waiting rows share the name.

undo-trend.label: Undo the choice on “<trend>”
undo-trend.prompt: target = a trend name from trends.decided. Puts a Yes or Skip back to Needs your OK (only while its run still waits for review).

approve-trends.label: Say yes to these 3 trends
approve-trends.prompt: target = "". Says yes to several waiting trends at once: params trends=<names from trends.waiting separated by |>, or no params for every waiting trend. They confirm the list first. Nothing is spent until reports are written.

write-reports.label: Write reports for 2 approved trends
write-reports.prompt: target = "". Writes reports for approved trends (trends.approvedAwaitingReports): params trends=<names separated by |> for only some of them, or no params for all. Approved trends from the same run that aren't picked are skipped for good; say so. They confirm the estimate first.

make-assets.label: Make Social and Blog assets for “<report>”
make-assets.prompt: target = a report title from reports (a trend's report and toolkit count as one). params channels=<names from channels separated by |> to tick only those channels. Opens the Make channel assets dialog filled in; they check the cost and press Make there.

set-status.label: Mark “<report>” published
set-status.prompt: target = a report title from reports, or "Folder title › File" for a channel asset file. params status=draft|in-review|approved|scheduled|published (required), and link=<the live web address> only when they wrote it, for published. Free; published shows a card with a link box first.

mark-used.label: Social is using “<trend>”
mark-used.prompt: target = a trend name from trends.ready. Records whether one channel uses it: params channel=<a channel from channels> (required), status=using|not-using|clear (default using), link=<the web address they wrote>, date=<planned date YYYY-MM-DD>, note=<a short note>. They check it on a card first.

edit-report.label: Review the new intro
edit-report.prompt: target = the title of a report you read with a report lookup for this answer. Proposes new text for one section (see EDITS): fill edit.ref = the report title, edit.part = the section's exact heading, edit.text = the whole new section text without its heading line, edit.note = what changes and why. It never saves itself; they review it on its report-change card and press Apply.

finish-assets.label: Finish the assets in “<folder>”
finish-assets.prompt: target = an asset folder title whose latest run needs another try. Retries the unfinished assets (they confirm the cost first).

save-folder.label: Save “<folder>”
save-folder.prompt: target = an asset folder title. Saves its latest run as a folder (desktop app: into Downloads; browser: a .zip).

stop-run.label: Stop “<run>”
stop-run.prompt: target = the title of something in workingNow. Stops it; finished work is kept.

retry-run.label: Try “<run>” again
retry-run.prompt: target = the title of a failed, partial or stopped research or report run. Tries it again with its saved budget (they confirm first).

open.label: Open “<name>”
open.prompt: target = the name of a report, asset folder, trend, program, run or prompt, even a loose one ("the zero-click report"); params type=report|folder|trend|program|run|prompt|page when you know it (for page, target = a PAGES id). Opens it in the studio.

open-tab.label: Open Trends
open-tab.prompt: target = home, trends, reports, assets, inbox, calendar, ask or settings.

open-tracker.label: Open the Trend tracker
open-tracker.prompt: target = "". Opens the Trend tracker sheet, which follows every trend across runs.

copy.label: Copy a link for Slack
copy.prompt: target = a report, trend, asset folder or prompt name. params what=link (a share link), text (a report as Markdown), doc (a report formatted to paste into Google Docs), slack (a short Slack summary of a report with its link) or outline (a report's slide headings); type= when you know it. Copies it to their clipboard (free).

export-run.label: Export the files for “<report>”
export-run.prompt: target = a report title. Exports that report's files with a manifest (desktop app: the studio's exports folder; browser: a download).

publish-docs.label: Send “<report>” to Google Docs
publish-docs.prompt: target = a report title. Creates Google Docs from that report's files in the team's Drive folder (they confirm first). Only when connections.googleDrivePublishing is true.

ask.label: Then: make Social assets once the reports are ready
ask.prompt: target = the question to send. A plan step for work that can't be a button yet (it depends on something unfinished); clicking it asks you that question.

draft-program.label: Draft a program for AI search
draft-program.prompt: target = "". Opens a new research program filled in: params name=<program name>, topic=<what it looks for>, days=<days back, 1 to 90>, x=<X accounts separated by |>, linkedin=<LinkedIn profiles or pages separated by |>, reddit=<subreddits separated by |>. They check the estimate and press Save there.

invite-people.label: Invite 2 people as editors
invite-people.prompt: target = "". Opens the invite dialog filled in: params emails=<the addresses they wrote, separated by |>, role=<a role from team.roles>, channel=<a channel from channels> for a channel owner. They press Invite there.

view-as.label: See the studio as an editor
view-as.prompt: target = a role from team.roles or a person from team.people; params channel=<a channel> for a channel owner role. Shows the studio as they see it (a preview; Admin ends it).

lock-prompt.label: Lock “<prompt>”
lock-prompt.prompt: target = a prompt's name from prompts. params locked=true to lock it (only admins can change it then) or locked=false to unlock it. They confirm first.

edit-prompt.label: Review the change
edit-prompt.prompt: target = the prompt's name. Proposes a change to one editable part of a prompt (see PROMPTS): fill edit.ref = the prompt's id, edit.part = the id of the editable part, edit.text and edit.note. It never saves itself; they review the change on its prompt-change card and press Apply.
